concedes: Lens 5 (tournament documents and formats). MTR 2.2 (play/draw rule) is two-player in wording: after each game 'the loser of that game' decides, and after a draw the player who decided at the drawn game chooses; it never addresses several losers. MTR 2.1 and 2.4 speak of 'one player'/'the other'. A search of the MTR for multiplayer finds only 7.2 (Conspiracy boosters, irrelevant), and its only multiplayer structure is Two-Headed Giant (section 9), where 9.3 has a team determined at random choose, with no loser rule, so no tournament rule settles which of several losers chooses. reference/formats/matches.md says the same: 'No official rule says who starts a later game or how a multiplayer match of several games ends', and the only community answer is level 4 (random first player each game), which cannot override a level 2 reading of CR 103.1 and does not contradict a gap-filling stipulation. commander.md defers to matches.md and sets no different start rule. So this is a genuine gap, no format or REL changes it, and the stipulation (earliest loser chooses; draw rule unchanged) contradicts no MTR or format text on the stated facts. Residual weaknesses that are not refutations: the user's confirm adds tie-break words (tied earliest losers decide between themselves, else random) that are not in the case's rule text, and teammates in Two-Headed Giant lose simultaneously, but that format has its own MTR 9.3 procedure for tournaments.
